editorial:
Imagine moving to a new city to start over after a bad breakup, only to realize your love life is still a total mess. That is exactly what you get with Armand, a quiet handyman living in Montreal. He is a great guy who just cannot seem to pick the right partner. You will watch him jump from one awkward relationship to another, including a brief fling with a younger woman and a confusing romance with a bored housewife. While he is trying to figure out his heart, his roommate is secretly pining for him, adding a layer of sweet but sad tension to the whole living situation. It is a gentle, human story that feels like watching a slice of real life unfold.

What really makes this work is how the acting feels natural and unforced. You will feel for Armand because his mistakes are things we have all done. The pacing is slow and relaxed, which might feel a bit long for some, but it helps you really connect with the characters. If you enjoy indie gems that focus on feelings rather than big explosions, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by showing that Armand is still searching for true stability. After his string of failed romances and the unspoken tension with his roommate, he learns that he cannot just fix his heart like he fixes a leaky faucet. The ending is more of a quiet realization than a big twist. He accepts his loneliness for a bit, hoping that by being honest with himself, he will eventually find a love that actually lasts.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves quiet character studies and realistic romance.
